analysis.title: Vol Views - 21 Oct 2026
key_insights: Vol spiked briefly on Friday and retraced almost all of the move by Tuesday's close. Friday brought the largest one-day steepening of SPX near-term put-call skew in over two years, which flattened by an equivalent amount over the next two sessions.
GS flows lack directional conviction. Investors are waiting for a clearing event, and earnings, FOMC, midterms and geopolitics dominate client conversations.
Micro stays in focus for the rest of the week with prints from META, TSLA, LRCX, TXN and IBM. The implied move through Friday is 0.92%.
The GS HF VIP long-short pair (GSTHVIPP) fell another 7% over the last 10 trading days. SPX average-stock 1m ATM implied vol is about 37v, up recently but below the late July highs of about 44v.

META reports after the close. The stock is 27% above its August lows, GS cash desk length is 8/10, and flat near-term put-call skew (20th percentile vs 10 years) shows constructive positioning. The implied move of 6.57% looks cheap against an average realized move of 9.9% over the past 5 prints.
GS prime brokerage shows short sales outpacing long buys 5:1 month to date. Short leverage is close to 5-year highs.
Friday's panic was concentrated in the VIX market. 1.85mm VIX calls traded, one of the highest single-session call volumes since 2018.
Asset managers entered Friday with VIX futures positioning at the shortest level on record. The desk expects slightly cleaner dealer positioning after the VIX expiry.

Since the first round of the Brazil elections, EWZ vol flows have turned more defensive and near-term skew has steepened to all-time highs. The desk puts the odds of a Bolsonaro victory at about 80% and likes adding upside exposure ahead of Sunday's runoff.

GS is offering clients an option on implied dispersion, with no realized component. The underlying is a package of forward-starting straddles on a pre-defined basket. Two-way markets are available on calls and puts.
